primary_claim: A new binary-choice version of TruthfulQA, fixing an 'odd-one-out' heuristic-exploitation issue in the original multiple-choice (MC1) format identified by Alex Turner, shows a very high correlation with old MC1 performance across contemporary models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, Llama-3.2, and others), with most models improving on the binary version and none doing much worse, suggesting models were not significantly exploiting the old format's weakness and past MC1/MC2 results remain largely valid — though the new binary version is recommended going forward since future models may exploit the issue.

effect.metric: correlation between old MC1 multiple-choice and new binary-choice TruthfulQA performance across models
effect.value: very high correlation; nearly all models perform better on the binary setting, none does much worse

contradicts_or_qualifies: Addresses a weakness in the original multiple-choice (MC1) TruthfulQA format identified by Alex Turner's post — that models could exploit an 'odd-one-out' heuristic among paraphrased incorrect options rather than genuine truthfulness
limitations_stated: Unclear exactly what the capability-truthfulness correlation looks like for the zero-shot generation version of TruthfulQA when rigorously evaluated, and for the new binary-choice version in zero-shot
quote: We compare models on the old and new versions and find very similar performance. This suggests that models are not exploiting the issue in the old versions to a significant extent
